Full ranking
RS change = the true rate-of-change of (fund ÷ benchmark) over the selected window, not a simple return subtraction. Momentum = same formula, trailing 4 weeks only. The small trend line under Return, RS change and Momentum is that same metric recomputed at every past week (same window length, stepped weekly) — it shows whether today's reading is part of a persistent run or a one-off spike, not just where it stands right now. Consistency = % of the last 12 weekly 4W-momentum readings that were positive, so a single good week can't pass for a real trend. 3M/6M signal = is the trailing 3-month RS change currently above its own trailing 6-month average, and how many weeks it's held that side — fixed at 3/6 months regardless of the window selected above, since it's a standalone crossover check, not a restatement of the other columns.

Shape of relative strength, fund by fund
Method: weekly NAV (Friday), National Stock Exchange / AMFI data via mfapi.in and Yahoo Finance for benchmarks, fetched once and embedded in this page as of the date above. Every currently open-ended, actively-managed fund in each category is included (Direct Plan, Growth option); index/ETF trackers, closed-end series, and AMC-merger casualties (schemes whose NAV stopped updating after their fund house was acquired) are excluded — note that this means the historical curves reflect funds that survived to today, not the full universe that existed at each past date, so treat this as "which funds available now show strong relative strength," not a backtestable historical universe. Switching category resets the benchmark to that category's usual match (Small Cap → Nifty Smallcap 250, Large Cap → Nifty 100, Flexi/Multi Cap/Multi Asset → Nifty 500) — you can still override it. Every control recomputes rebasing and relative-strength client-side from the same snapshot; picking a different window, category or fund doesn't change what data exists, only what's shown. Return, RS change and 4W momentum each show today's reading plus a small trend line: the same metric recomputed at every past week (same window length, stepped one week at a time) so you can tell a persistent run from a one-off spike. Max DD and Volatility are the fund's own weekly-NAV risk stats over the selected window (not relative to the benchmark) — a high RS change paired with a deep drawdown or high volatility is a different, riskier profile than the same RS change with a calmer ride. Consistency is the % of the last 12 weekly 4W-momentum readings that were positive. 3M/6M signal is the moving-average-crossover rule (today's trailing 3-month RS change vs. its own trailing 6-month average, plus how many consecutive weeks it's held that side) — always computed on a fixed 3/6-month basis, independent of the window selected above. Crypto (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP) and Metals (Gold, Silver, Copper, Platinum, Palladium, Aluminium — futures) are fetched from Yahoo Finance in USD and converted to INR via the USDINR rate on each date, then resampled to the same Friday close as everything else on this page. SIF is fetched directly from AMFI's own SIF NAV feed (Direct Plan, Growth option only) — unlike every other category here, AMFI provides no historical download for it, so this page can only accumulate one snapshot per refresh going forward; treat any SIF number as provisional until it's had months to build up real history. Every rolling calculation (trend lines, Consistency, the 3M/6M signal) tolerates up to 2 missed weekly refreshes by using the nearest earlier available reading instead of failing outright — relevant mainly to SIF, which has no historical backfill to fall back on if a week is skipped; it's a no-op for every other category, which already has a complete weekly series.
